newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon finance group to meet in U.S. December 16.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon finance group to meet in U.S. December 16.

text.p: A consultative group of nations to help finance Lebanon's postwar reconstruction will hold its first meeting in Washington on December 16, Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri was quoted on Sunday as saying.

The agreement was reached at talks between Hariri and U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday at the White House, Hariri was quoted by al-Anwar daily as telling a press conference in Washington on Saturday.

"It was agreed that December 16 will be the date for the consultative committee to meet in Washington. This is a positive thing and a clear indicator of the United States of America's help to Lebanon and its support to its rebuilding," he said.

The committee being formed by the United States includes France, the European Union, Russia and other countries. It was set up in April under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz against Lebanon.
Acting Finance Minister Fouad Siniora, who accompanied Hariri to Washington, has said Beirut will ask the committee for $5 billion over five years in soft loans and donations.
Hariri said Clinton will send letters to the "friendly countries" to attend the meeting.
Siniora was quoted by al-Anwar as saying that the committee will also group Canada, Brazil, Gulf Arab states, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia and "other countries which are being contacted at present".
